short_description: 9 printable tools for ages 2–5: picture checklists, together tokens, helping jobs, a family plan and a 30-day tracker. Fillable PDF, Letter + A4.
long_description:
The Play-First Family Kit for ages 2–5 has 9 printable tools, in a PDF you can type in: picture checklists, tokens, helping jobs and a family plan. It gives your day a kind shape: jobs first, then play and time together, then screens at their usual spot. Nothing is taken away; there's just more play.

The Play First, Then Screens checklist comes with big pictures for ages 2–5 and as a fillable blank. Each has 4 colorways and a Monday or Sunday start. Little ones also get a helping-jobs chart and a first-then-later Play-First Board.

The whole family gets 24 together tokens (12 ready-made, 12 blank) and six screen-spot cards, such as "5 more minutes" and "what we do next." There is a rules poster and a three-page Family Play & Screen Plan. A 30-day tracker holds 30 plays that need nothing to buy. Each has a starting age, easier and harder ways and a 2-minute version. A certificate marks the end.

Tokens are for play and time together, never screen minutes. The screen spot stays the same every day. A two-page grown-up guide covers a 2-minute setup, three talk lines and how it works from 2 to 5, plus printing, laminating and velcro tips. Every play follows our published safety rules.

You get color and low-ink files in US Letter and A4, with type-in fields for free Adobe Acrobat Reader. Instant download; nothing ships.

A color checklist and a “Little helping jobs” page, with two together tokens, Story together and Dance party. Labels: fillable PDF, US Letter and A4, 4 colorways.

What’s inside: 9 tools in one download, 41 pages. Tiles for: Play First, Then Screens checklists (16 pages); the Play-First Board (first, then, later); Little helping jobs; Together tokens (12 plus 12 blank); screen-spot cards; the Family Play Rules poster; the Family Play and Screen Plan; 30 Days of Play First; and a certificate.

A 2-minute grown-up guide: plain words, no lectures. Two guide pages, “Start here, grown-ups” and “How it works at each age”: set up in 2 minutes, three easy talk lines, and screens keep one steady spot in the day.

Play First, Then Screens checklist: 4 colorways, Monday or Sunday start. Four checklist pages labelled Ages 2–5 tomato, Sunday start sky, Fillable grass and Sunday start plum. Big pictures for ages 2–5, plus a fillable blank to make your own.

Ages 2–5: Little helping jobs and the Play-First Board. A page of picture jobs such as feed the pet, water plants and match socks, and the board: 1, first, jobs; 2, then, together time; 3, later, screens. Every cut piece is at least 2.1 in (5.3 cm), bigger than the toilet-paper-tube test; a grown-up keeps the pieces.

For the whole family: Our Family Play & Screen Plan. Three fill-in plan pages and the Our Family Play Rules poster, with rules such as “We play first,” “Screens have a spot in our day” and “Grown-ups play too.”

Together tokens and 30 Days of Play: tokens are for play, never screen minutes. Three token cards, Story together, Board game and Sing together, and the 30 Days of Play First tracker with a picture for each day’s play. Every play has an age and a 2-minute version.

Sizes and formats: fillable, printable, your way. A color checklist and the same checklist in low-ink line art. Notes: fillable in free Adobe Acrobat Reader on a computer or phone; you can edit text boxes (names, dates, jobs, rules, token ideas, plan answers) but not colors or pictures; pre-filled and blank pages; US Letter and A4; color plus low-ink; 5 files, START HERE plus 4 PDFs.

How to use: print, fill, play. Four steps: download in a web browser, not the Etsy app; fill in (optional) in free Adobe Acrobat Reader; print at 100%, charts on paper and tokens, cards and the board on cardstock, about 20 minutes to prep; laminate or use page protectors, with velcro for ages 3 and up only. A digital download: no physical item ships.

compliance_notes: Parent education only; no health, medical or developmental-outcome claims, no therapy, diagnosis or condition wording anywhere, including keywords and tags (BRAND hard rule 1 and the diagnosis-search rule). No named device brands, apps, companies or schools; only a generic sleeping tablet appears as a neutral object. Screens have a fixed spot that never grows or shrinks with jobs or behavior, and tokens are for play and connection only, never screen minutes; together time is never taken away as a punishment (CUSTOMER-VOICE rule 26, conflict #1 resolved as recommended). A talker (a device a child uses to talk) is named as the child's voice, not screen time, on the guide and plan pages (rule 28). No-guilt test applied: no fear words, 'some days need more screens, and that's okay'. Citations used: WHO 2019 under-5 guidelines and AAP 'Media and Young Minds' 2016 only (BRAND rule 5); the family-plan guideline box attributes to AAP only what 'Media and Young Minds' says (co-viewing, 1 hour of high-quality programs at 2–5, screen-free times and places, a family plan), and gives no number for older children. Child safety (rule 4): every cut piece is 2.1 in (5.3 cm) or larger (check.js measures the smallest: 2.100 in), straight-line grid cutting, 12 pieces or fewer per page, 'Grown-up keeps the pieces' on every cut sheet, velcro for ages 3+ only with 'check dots before each play; remove any that lift', an actual-size print check on the tips page, a grown-up nearby for every play, and a 3-page play guide that gives each of the 30 plays a starting age in months, prep, mess and play-time labels, make it easier / make it harder, a 2-minute tired-grown-up version and its own safety line (small toys and blocks bigger than a toilet-paper tube for under-3s, no whole grapes, nuts, popcorn or hard candy for under-4s, no cords or long scarves around necks, a grown-up holds bubbles and tape, pretend or cool water for tea parties, no-hide places for hide and seek) (CUSTOMER-VOICE rules 4, 6, 7), water/bubbles/cooking within arm's reach, grown-ups handle knives, heat and glass; no balloons, cords or choking foods. Listing says 'Every play follows our published safety rules' and never 'safety-checked' or 'safe for all ages'. Copyright line and 'Version 1.0 · September 2026' in every page footer; license 'Personal & family use'. Etsy edition (etsy-upload/ and all listing images) carries no URL or QR code (gate #16); own-store edition carries playbeforepixels.com in footers and the bonus QR on the last page and START HERE. Honest pricing: no 'was' price. PDFs are tagged, bookmarked and under 15 MB each. Color is never the only signal (age chips carry word labels; low-ink chips add shapes). Contrast (gate #20): no small white text sits on tomato, sky or grass; the checklist band keeps only 28 pt and 14 pt bold white type (large text, 3:1 or better), and number badges use ink numerals. Devices: only the generic sleeping tablet appears (no phone).

faq.q: What's inside, and do I have to use it all?
faq.a: 9 tools for ages 2–5 in a color file and a low-ink file, US Letter and A4. Most families use 2 or 3 of them; start with the checklist.

faq.q: Does my child have to earn screen time?
faq.a: No. Screens have the same spot every day, whatever happens with jobs or behavior. Together tokens are for play and time together, never screen minutes.

faq.q: My child uses a talker (a device to talk). Does it count as a screen?
faq.a: No. A talker is your child's voice, so it stays with them at meals, in the car and at night. The guide and the family plan both say so.
Ages 2–5. Big pictures for little ones, and blanks you can fill in for any age. Every one of the 30 plays shows a starting age in months. Ages are a guide, never a deadline.

faq.q: Can I give it as a gift?
faq.a: Yes. Buy it and forward the download email to the family, or print it for them. The personal license then belongs to that family.

faq.q: Can grandparents or a sitter use it?
faq.a: Yes. The personal license covers grandparents and sitters who care for your child. Take the board and tokens along; the safety notes on page 5 go with them.

faq.q: Can a classroom, child-care center, library or PTA use it?
faq.a: Not yet. This kit is licensed for personal and family use in your own home. Classroom, center, library and group licenses are not available yet.
